clinician.final_diagnosis: Emphysematous pyelonephritis complicated by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old non-diabetic woman presented to the emergency department with acute-on-chronic right knee, left hip, and paraspinal lumbar back pain progressing over one week, accompanied by pursed-lip breathing and urinary retention. Initial vital signs were stable. CT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis on admission revealed a prominent left renal staghorn calculus with suspicious intraparenchymal gas locules, consistent with emphysematous pyelonephritis (EPN). The patient rapidly deteriorated, becoming tachycardic and febrile with early signs of shock. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin and Zosyn) were initiated, and the patient was taken emergently to the operating room where percutaneous nephrostomy tube placement was performed by urology and interventional radiology. Post-operative urinalysis revealed large amounts of blood, positive leukocyte esterase, and Escherichia coli urinary tract infection. During hospitalization, the patient developed acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring prolonged intubation in the intensive care unit. The clinical presentation of emphysematous pyelonephritis with rapid septic deterioration, combined with the imaging findings of gas in the renal parenchyma and the documented E. coli UTI, supports the final diagnosis of emphysematous pyelonephritis complicated by MRSA bacteremia.

final.final_diagnosis: Emphysematous pyelonephritis complicated by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia
final.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old non-diabetic woman presented to the emergency department with acute-on-chronic right knee, left hip, and paraspinal lumbar back pain progressing over one week, accompanied by pursed-lip breathing and urinary retention. Initial vital signs were stable. CT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis on admission revealed a prominent left renal staghorn calculus with suspicious intraparenchymal gas locules, consistent with emphysematous pyelonephritis (EPN). The patient rapidly deteriorated, becoming tachycardic and febrile with early signs of shock. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin and Zosyn) were initiated, and the patient was taken emergently to the operating room where percutaneous nephrostomy tube placement was performed by urology and interventional radiology. Post-operative urinalysis revealed large amounts of blood, positive leukocyte esterase, and Escherichia coli urinary tract infection. During hospitalization, the patient developed acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring prolonged intubation in the intensive care unit. The clinical presentation of emphysematous pyelonephritis with rapid septic deterioration, combined with the imaging findings of gas in the renal parenchyma and the documented E. coli UTI, supports the final diagnosis of emphysematous pyelonephritis complicated by MRSA bacteremia.
